metadata.title: Certified mathematical identities of the K₇ framework: E₈×E₈ gauge theory on a G₂-holonomy manifold, 460+ relations, 0 sorry, Lean 4. Formerly gift-framework/core (GIFT Core). Distinct from Arithmon/Lean, the Sieve methodology layer.

nodes.name: Standard Euclidean Space
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{R}^8$ denote the 8-dimensional Euclidean space with standard inner product.
nodes.label: def:R8

nodes.name: Standard Basis
nodes.statement: The standard basis vectors $e_i$ for $i \in \{0, \ldots, 7\}$ satisfy $\langle e_i, e_j \rangle = \delta_{ij}$.
nodes.label: def:stdBasis

nodes.name: Basis Orthonormality
nodes.statement: For all $i, j \in \{0, \ldots, 7\}$: \[ \langle e_i, e_j \rangle = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]
nodes.label: thm:stdBasis_orthonormal

nodes.name: Inner Product Sum
nodes.statement: For $v, w \in \mathbb{R}^8$: $\langle v, w \rangle = \sum_{i=0}^{7} v_i w_i$
nodes.label: thm:inner_eq_sum

nodes.name: Integer Coordinates
nodes.statement: A vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^8$ has \emph{all integer coordinates} if $v_i \in \mathbb{Z}$ for all $i$.
nodes.label: def:AllInteger

nodes.name: Half-Integer Coordinates
nodes.statement: A vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^8$ has \emph{all half-integer coordinates} if $v_i \in \mathbb{Z} + \frac{1}{2}$ for all $i$.
nodes.label: def:AllHalfInteger

nodes.name: Even Sum
nodes.statement: A vector $v$ has \emph{even sum} if $\sum_{i=0}^{7} v_i \in 2\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.label: def:SumEven

nodes.name: E8 Lattice
nodes.statement: The $E_8$ lattice consists of all $v \in \mathbb{R}^8$ satisfying either: \begin{enumerate} \item All coordinates are integers with even sum, or \item All coordinates are half-integers with even sum \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:E8_lattice

nodes.statement: Case analysis on integer/half-integer coordinates with parity arguments.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:sum_sq_mod_two}, sum of squared integers has same parity as sum. For half-integers, $\sum(n_i + 1/2)^2 = \sum n_i^2 + \sum n_i + 2$, which is even.

nodes.name: Weyl Reflection
nodes.statement: For a root $\alpha$ with $\langle \alpha, \alpha \rangle = 2$, the Weyl reflection is: \[ s_\alpha(v) = v - \langle v, \alpha \rangle \cdot \alpha \]
nodes.label: def:E8_reflection

nodes.statement: Since $\langle v, \alpha \rangle \in \mathbb{Z}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:E8_inner_integral} and $E_8$ is closed under integer scaling and subtraction.

nodes.name: Fano Line Count
nodes.statement: The Fano plane has exactly 7 lines.
nodes.label: thm:fano_lines_count

nodes.name: Epsilon Tensor
nodes.statement: The structure constants $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ for the 7D cross product: \begin{itemize} \item $\varepsilon_{ijk} = +1$ for $(i,j,k)$ a cyclic permutation of a Fano line \item $\varepsilon_{ijk} = -1$ for anticyclic permutations \item $\varepsilon_{ijk} = 0$ otherwise \end{itemize}
nodes.label: def:epsilon

nodes.name: 7D Cross Product
nodes.statement: For $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^7$, the cross product is: \[ (u \times v)_k = \sum_{i,j} \varepsilon_{ijk} \, u_i \, v_j \]
nodes.label: def:cross

nodes.name: Cross Product Bilinearity
nodes.statement: The cross product is bilinear: \begin{align} (au + v) \times w &= a(u \times w) + v \times w \\ u \times (av + w) &= a(u \times v) + u \times w \end{align}
nodes.label: thm:G2_cross_bilinear

nodes.name: Coassociative 4-form
nodes.statement: The 7D correction to the Kronecker formula: \[ \psi_{ijlm} = \sum_k \varepsilon_{ijk}\varepsilon_{lmk} - (\delta_{il}\delta_{jm} - \delta_{im}\delta_{jl}) \]
nodes.label: def:psi

nodes.statement: Antisymmetric tensor $\psi$ contracted with symmetric $u_i u_l$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Lagrange Identity
nodes.statement: \[ \| u \times v \|^2 = \| u \|^2 \| v \|^2 - \langle u, v \rangle^2 \]
nodes.label: thm:G2_cross_norm

nodes.statement: Expand $\|u \times v\|^2$ via coordinate sums. The $\varepsilon$-contraction decomposes into Kronecker deltas plus $\psi_{ijlm}$ terms. By antisymmetry of $\psi$ (verified for all 2401 cases), the $\psi$-terms vanish under symmetric contraction $u_i u_l v_j v_m$. The Kronecker terms yield $\|u\|^2 \|v\|^2 - \langle u,v \rangle^2$.

nodes.name: SO(16) Spinor
nodes.statement: The chiral spinor of $\mathrm{SO}(16)$ has dimension $2^8/2 = 128$.
nodes.label: def:spinor_SO16

nodes.name: Geometric Part
nodes.statement: The geometric part encodes K$_7$ topology: \[ \mathrm{geom} = b_2 + b_3 + \mathrm{dim}(G_2) + \mathrm{rank}(E_8) = 21 + 77 + 14 + 8 \]
nodes.label: def:geometric_part

nodes.name: Spinorial = 128
nodes.statement: The spinorial part equals the $\mathrm{SO}(16)$ spinor dimension.
nodes.label: thm:spinorial_is_128

nodes.name: Gauge-Fermion Split
nodes.statement: Physical interpretation: \begin{itemize} \item 120 = topology + holonomy + Cartan $\to$ \textbf{gauge bosons} \item 128 = $2^7$ from octonions $\to$ \textbf{fermions} \end{itemize}
nodes.label: thm:gauge_fermion_split

nodes.name: Historical Context
nodes.statement: The Koide formula $Q = 2/3$ was discovered empirically in 1981 and remained unexplained for 43 years. GIFT derives it in two lines from topology.

nodes.name: Spectral Index Indices
nodes.statement: The spectral index $n_s = \zeta(11)/\zeta(5)$ uses: \begin{itemize} \item $11 = D_{\mathrm{bulk}}$ (M-theory dimension) \item $5 = $ Weyl factor \end{itemize}
nodes.label: thm:n_s_indices

nodes.name: Joyce Complete Certificate
nodes.statement: All conditions verified: topological ($b_2 = 21$, $b_3 = 77$), analytic (contraction mapping), existence.
nodes.label: thm:joyce_cert

nodes.name: Standard G2 Form
nodes.statement: The standard associative 3-form $\varphi_0 = \sum_{ijk} \varepsilon_{ijk}\, dx^i \wedge dx^j \wedge dx^k$ where $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ are the Fano plane structure constants, normalized for $\det(g) = 65/32$.
nodes.label: def:phi0_standard

nodes.name: G2 Adjoint Perturbation
nodes.statement: The PINN parameterizes perturbations via the 14-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}_2$ adjoint: \[ \varphi(x) = \varphi_0 + \delta\varphi(x), \quad \delta\varphi \in \mathfrak{g}_2 \] Only 14 functions are learned (not 35).
nodes.label: def:delta_phi

nodes.name: Dimension Reduction
nodes.statement: The G2 constraint reduces parameters from 35 to 14: $35 - 14 = 21 = b_2$
nodes.label: thm:dim_reduction

nodes.name: Joyce Condition
nodes.statement: The PINN torsion is well below Joyce threshold: $0.001 < 0.0288$
nodes.label: thm:joyce_satisfied

nodes.name: Fourier Coefficients
nodes.statement: The trained PINN is evaluated on a grid and FFT identifies dominant modes. Coefficients are rationalized to $\mathbb{Q}$ within tolerance $10^{-8}$.
nodes.label: def:fourier_coeffs

nodes.name: Target in Interval
nodes.statement: The target value $65/32$ lies in the certified interval for $\det(g)$.
nodes.label: thm:target_interval

nodes.name: Seven Terms
nodes.statement: $\varphi_0$ has exactly 7 non-zero terms (of 35 independent components).
nodes.label: thm:phi0_seven

nodes.name: C(7,3) Components
nodes.statement: A 3-form on $\mathbb{R}^7$ has $\binom{7}{3} = 35$ independent components, indexed lexicographically: $(0,1,2) \mapsto 0$, $(0,1,3) \mapsto 1$, etc.
nodes.label: def:35_components

nodes.name: Scale Factor
nodes.statement: To achieve $\det(g) = 65/32$, we scale $\varphi_0$ by: \[ c = \left(\frac{65}{32}\right)^{1/14} \approx 1.0543 \]
nodes.label: def:scale_c

nodes.name: Scaling Derivation
nodes.statement: For $\varphi = c \cdot \varphi_0$ and metric $g_{ij} = \frac{1}{6}\sum_{k,l} \varphi_{ikl}\varphi_{jkl}$: \begin{enumerate} \item Standard $\varphi_0$ gives $g = I_7$, so $\det(g) = 1$ \item Scaling $\varphi \mapsto c \cdot \varphi$ gives $g \mapsto c^2 \cdot g$ \item Therefore $\det(g) \mapsto c^{14} \cdot \det(g)$ \item Setting $c^{14} = 65/32$ yields $\det(g) = 65/32$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:scale_derivation

nodes.name: Scaled Identity Metric
nodes.statement: The induced metric is: \[ g = c^2 \cdot I_7 = \left(\frac{65}{32}\right)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \approx 1.1115 \cdot I_7 \] Explicitly: \[ g_{ij} = \begin{cases} (65/32)^{1/7} & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]
nodes.label: thm:metric_form

nodes.name: Zero Torsion
nodes.statement: For a constant 3-form $\varphi(x) = \varphi_0$: \begin{itemize} \item $d\varphi = 0$ (exterior derivative of constant) \item $d{*}\varphi = 0$ (same reasoning) \end{itemize} Therefore $T = 0$ \textbf{exactly}.
nodes.label: thm:torsion_zero

nodes.name: Analytical G2 Metric
nodes.statement: The canonical GIFT G2 metric on $K_7$ is given by: \textbf{3-form} ($35$ components, $7$ non-zero): \[ \varphi_i = \begin{cases} +c & i \in \{0, 9, 14, 20\} \\ -c & i \in \{23, 27, 28\} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \] where $c = (65/32)^{1/14}$. \textbf{Metric} ($7 \times 7$ diagonal): \[ g = (65/32)^{1/7} \cdot I_7 \] \textbf{Properties}: \begin{itemize} \item $\det(g) = 65/32$ (exact) \item $\|T\| = 0$ (torsion-free) \item $\mathrm{Hol}(g) = G_2$ (by construction) \end{itemize}
nodes.label: thm:analytical_metric

nodes.name: Simplicity
nodes.statement: This is the \emph{simplest possible} G2 structure satisfying GIFT constraints. The solution is a constant 3-form with only 7 non-zero components and a diagonal metric. No PINN training or Fourier analysis is required---the standard G2 form is the answer.

nodes.name: G2 vs Fano
nodes.statement: The G2 3-form indices are \textbf{different} from Fano plane lines: \begin{align*} \text{G2 3-form:} &\quad (0,1,2), (0,3,4), (0,5,6), (1,3,5), (1,4,6), (2,3,6), (2,4,5) \\ \text{Fano lines:} &\quad (0,1,3), (1,2,4), (2,3,5), (3,4,6), (4,5,0), (5,6,1), (6,0,2) \end{align*} Both have 7 terms but represent different structures (3-form vs cross-product).

nodes.name: Chebyshev Order
nodes.statement: The Chebyshev polynomial order $K = 5$, giving $K + 1 = 6$ modes.
nodes.label: def:chebyshev_K

nodes.name: Cholesky Entries
nodes.statement: A $7 \times 7$ lower-triangular matrix has $\binom{8}{2} = 28$ independent entries.
nodes.label: def:cholesky_entries

nodes.name: Off-diagonal = $b_2$
nodes.statement: The 21 off-diagonal Cholesky entries equal $b_2(K_7)$, reflecting the $b_2$-dimensional moduli space of $G_2$ structures.
nodes.label: thm:cholesky_offdiag_b2

nodes.name: 169 Total Parameters

nodes.name: $169 = 13^2 = \alpha_{\mathrm{sum}}^2$

nodes.name: $168 = |\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)|$
nodes.statement: The Chebyshev parameter count $168 = |\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)|$, the Fano automorphism group.

nodes.name: det$(g) = 65/32$
nodes.statement: The metric satisfies $\det(g) = 65/32$ at every evaluation point, with $\gcd(65, 32) = 1$.

nodes.name: PINN Compression $> 6000\times$

nodes.name: K3 NK master certificate
nodes.statement: Six-conjunct master certificate: both $\beta$ sources pass, $k=2$ fails, $\eta_{L^2} < 2/100$, parameter count $> 10{,}000$, and $\delta_{K3}^{\mathrm{cert}} < \varepsilon_0 = 0.1$ (Joyce threshold).
nodes.label: thm:k3_nk_master

nodes.name: Alternating telescope
nodes.statement: For all $n$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} (-1)^k \binom{3/2}{k} = (-1)^n \binom{1/2}{n}$. Combined with $|\binom{1/2}{n}| \leq 1/(2n-1)$, this is the elementary engine for the two main results, used in place of any boundary-limit theorem.
nodes.label: lem:collar_telescope

nodes.name: Absolute re-summation $\sum |\binom{3/2}{k}| = 3$
nodes.statement: The absolute generalized-binomial series is summable with $\sum_{k \geq 0} |\binom{3/2}{k}| = 3$: the collar bound erodes the bulk bound by exactly the factor $3$, independently of the adiabatic parameter.
nodes.label: thm:collar_resum

nodes.name: Alternating value without Abel
nodes.statement: $\sum_{k \geq 0} (-1)^k \binom{3/2}{k} = 0$, i.e. the binomial series of $(1+x)^{3/2}$ evaluated at $x = -1$, obtained here without any boundary-limit theorem.
nodes.label: thm:alt_binomial

nodes.name: Indicial parity $K_{\mathrm{ind}}(-1) = K_{\mathrm{ind}}(+1) = 4/3$
nodes.statement: Since $P_m$ is even in $\beta$, the indicial constant $K_{\mathrm{ind}}(\beta) = 1/|P_{1/2}(\beta)|$ satisfies $K_{\mathrm{ind}}(-1) = K_{\mathrm{ind}}(+1) = 4/3$: the weighted-Schauder constant carries verbatim across the $\beta = +1$ and $\beta = -1$ weights.
nodes.label: thm:indicial_parity

nodes.name: TCS Manifold
nodes.statement: A TCS manifold $K = M_1 \cup_N M_2$ consists of: \begin{itemize} \item Two asymptotically cylindrical manifolds $M_1, M_2$ (building blocks) \item A cylindrical neck $N \cong Y \times [0, L]$ with cross-section $Y$ \item Neck length parameter $L > 0$ \item Volume normalization: $\mathrm{Vol}(K) = 1$ \end{itemize}
nodes.label: def:TCSManifold

nodes.name: TCS Hypotheses Bundle
nodes.statement: The six hypotheses (H1)--(H6) for spectral bounds: \begin{enumerate} \item[(H1)] Volume normalization: $\mathrm{Vol}(K) = 1$ \item[(H2)] Bounded neck volume: $v_0 \leq \mathrm{Vol}(N) \leq v_1$ \item[(H3)] Product metric: $g|_N = dt^2 + g_Y$ \item[(H4)] Block Cheeger bound: $h(M_i \setminus N) \geq h_0$ \item[(H5)] Balanced blocks: $\mathrm{Vol}(M_i) \in [1/4, 3/4]$ \item[(H6)] Neck minimality: $\mathrm{Area}(\Gamma) \geq \mathrm{Area}(Y)$ \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:TCSHypotheses

nodes.name: TCS Spectral Bounds
nodes.statement: For TCS manifold $K$ with neck length $L > L_0$ satisfying (H1)--(H6): \[ \frac{c_1}{L^2} \leq \lambda_1(K) \leq \frac{c_2}{L^2} \]
nodes.label: thm:tcs_spectral_bounds

nodes.name: Inverse Square Scaling
nodes.statement: The spectral gap scales as $\lambda_1 = \Theta(1/L^2)$ as $L \to \infty$.
nodes.label: thm:inverse_L_squared

nodes.name: Typical Parameter Values
nodes.statement: For typical TCS with $v_0 = v_1 = 1/2$, $h_0 = 1$: \begin{itemize} \item $c_1 = 1/4$ \item $c_2 = 16$ \item $L_0 = 1$ \item Bound ratio: $c_2/c_1 = 64$ \end{itemize}
nodes.label: thm:typical_tcs

nodes.name: Cross-Section
nodes.statement: Cross-section of TCS cylindrical end with dimension and Betti numbers.
nodes.label: def:CrossSection

nodes.name: K3 x S1 Cross-Section
nodes.statement: Standard Kovalev construction with $\dim = 5$ and $b_0 = 1, b_1 = 1, b_2 = 22, b_3 = 22, b_4 = 23, b_5 = 1$.
nodes.label: def:K3_S1

nodes.name: Langlais Spectral Density
nodes.statement: For TCS family $(M_T, g_T)$ with cross-section $X$: \[ \Lambda_q(s) = 2(b_{q-1}(X) + b_q(X))\sqrt{s} + O(1) \] Reference: Langlais 2024, Comm. Math. Phys.
nodes.label: thm:langlais

nodes.name: CGN No Small Eigenvalues
nodes.statement: For TCS manifold with neck length $L$: $\exists c > 0$ such that no eigenvalues in $(0, c/L)$. Reference: Crowley-Goette-Nordstrom 2024, Inventiones Math.
nodes.label: thm:cgn_no_small

nodes.name: GIFT Prediction Structure
nodes.statement: The bare ratio $14/99 = \dim(G_2)/H^*$ is consistent with TCS bounds: $1/100 < 14/99 < 1/4$.
nodes.label: thm:gift_prediction

nodes.name: TCS Bounds Certificate
nodes.statement: Complete verification of TCS spectral bounds and GIFT prediction compatibility.
nodes.label: thm:tcs_certificate

nodes.name: Three-Level Derivation
nodes.statement: The physical spectral gap $\lambda_1 = 13/99$ emerges from three levels: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Model Theorem} (PROVEN): $\lambda_1 \sim 1/L^2$ from TCS geometry \item \textbf{Canonical Length} (CONJECTURE): $L^2 \sim H^* = 99$ from volume principle \item \textbf{Holonomy Coefficient} (PROVEN): $\mathrm{dim}(G_2) - h = 14 - 1 = 13$ (Berger) \end{itemize} The bare ratio $14/99$ receives a correction of $-1/99 = -h/H^*$ from the parallel spinor (see Chapter~\ref{chap:physical_spectral}).

nodes.name: G2 Parallel Spinors
nodes.statement: $G_2$-holonomy manifolds admit exactly $h = 1$ parallel spinor (Berger classification; Joyce 2000, Table~10.1).
nodes.label: def:parallel_spinors_G2

nodes.name: Physical Gap Numerator
nodes.statement: The physical mass gap numerator: $\mathrm{dim}(G_2) - h = 14 - 1 = 13$.
nodes.label: def:physical_gap_num

nodes.name: Physical Gap from Topology
nodes.statement: $13/99 = (\mathrm{dim}(G_2) - h) / H^*$ where all quantities are topological.
nodes.label: thm:physical_gap_topology

nodes.name: Irreducibility
nodes.statement: $\gcd(13, 99) = 1$. The ratio $13/99$ is in lowest terms.
nodes.label: thm:physical_gap_irreducible

nodes.name: Bare to Physical Correction
nodes.statement: $14/99 - 13/99 = 1/99 = h/H^*$. The correction is exactly the parallel spinor count divided by the total cohomological dimension.
nodes.label: thm:bare_minus_physical

nodes.name: Cross-Holonomy: SU(3)
nodes.statement: For $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ holonomy: $\mathrm{dim}(\mathrm{SU}(3)) - h = 8 - 2 = 6$. Numerically validated: $\lambda_1 \times H^* = 5.996$ on $T^6/\mathbb{Z}_3$.
nodes.label: thm:SU3_spectral

nodes.name: Pell Equation
nodes.statement: $99^2 - 50 \times 14^2 = 1$. The bare topological constants $(14, 99)$ satisfy a Pell equation with discriminant $50 = 2 \times 5^2$.
nodes.label: thm:pell_equation

nodes.name: Bieberbach Bound

nodes.name: SPD$_7$ Dimension

nodes.name: SPD$_7$ = Twice Holonomy
